narration: It was a night when the stars shone beautifully. I remember a boy once standing atop a hill on a night like this. It is a memory so distant it feels more like a half-forgotten dream.

I used to hate the night. Nightfall brought a specific kind of silence—one that felt heavy and sharp with cold. I’d slip between the frozen sheets, feeling the vast, ink-black space of the room pressing in on me. Even with my eyelids squeezed shut, the darkness felt alive, keeping rest just out of reach.  I would brace myself against the dark and pray for the morning to come.

One night, a strange light flickered against my eyelids. It felt different from the usual pale shimmer of the moon. Driven by curiosity, I opened my eyes. Outside my window, a single beam of light descended from the heavens like a silken thread, landing on a remote hill at the edge of town.
I watched until the glow began to fade. By the time I rubbed my sleepy eyes, it was gone. Still half-dreaming, I slipped out of the house and made my way toward the outskirts of town.

As I climbed the hill, I saw him—a boy who looked to be about my age. Despite the summer season, the air at this altitude turned biting once the sun went down. Yet, he wore nothing but a single layer of tattered, thin clothes. He didn't seem to feel the cold at all.

"Hello there," he said.
He raised a hand in greeting the moment he saw me cresting the ridge. His simple, honest smile instantly dissolved my wariness. I ended up staying there with him until the sun rose. After that night, I found myself returning to the hill again and again just to see him.
